title: Invocation resilience eval plan — arg parsing & multi-step flows
summary: Proposal for a lightweight but actionable evaluation suite to catch regressions in tool selection and argument parsing for models being onboarded. Focused on multi-step flows and resilience under noisy prompts and truncated contexts.
body:
Context:
- We are onboarding ModelX-v2 (quantized variant) into hosted + dedicated paths. Early integration noted occasional tool-selection flips and malformed arg payloads when the model is used in multistep conversational flows. This doc lays out a reproducible eval plan to surface those failure modes pre-rollout and to act as a gate for Dedicated capacity profile changes.

Goals:
1) Detect regressions that meaningfully change tool-selection accuracy (>2.5% absolute) on our canonical prompt sets.
2) Catch arg-parsing errors that lead to invalid function payloads or silent fallbacks (target: arg-parse F1 drop >=5% triggers investigation).
3) Measure end-to-end multi-step flow success rate (E2E-SR) under synthetic noise and truncated context.
4) Provide a prioritized set of failing transcripts and a triage rubric for engineers.

Non-goals:
- Exhaustive coverage of every tool in the product. This is a targeted resilience scan for the most-used tool set (search, calendar, http-fetch, db-read).

Scope and test corpus:
- Baseline canonical prompts: 300 manually curated prompts derived from customer telemetry (anonymized) covering tool invocation, ambiguous tool hints, and explicit function calls.
- Compositional multi-step flows: 120 scenarios where tool outputs feed back into prompts. Includes 2-8 step chains.
- Noise variants: For each canonical prompt, generate 3 perturbations: word-drop (10% token removal), filler-noise (insert disfluent tokens like "uh", "one sec"), and truncation (drop last 30% of context).
- Edge fuzzers: 500 synthetic mutation cases for argument forms (JSON-like but malformed quoting/commas, nested lists vs flat lists, numeric vs string types).
- Latency/throughput sweep: run subset under batch sizes [1,4,8] to detect behavior differences introduced by batching.

Metrics (primary):
- Tool Selection Accuracy (TSA): fraction of invocations where selected tool matches gold label.
- Arg Parse Precision/Recall/F1: compare parsed function arguments to gold argument structure. Token-level and field-level F1.
- E2E Success Rate (E2E-SR): fraction of multi-step flows that produce a final correct result (vetted by simple automated checker).
- Silent Fallback Rate: fraction of cases where model returns natural-language instead of structured call when call expected.
- Latency distribution: p50/p95 response times under the sweep.

Pass/fail thresholds (proposal):
- TSA drop > 2.5% relative to baseline => FAIL.
- Arg parse F1 drop > 5 points absolute => FAIL.
- E2E-SR drop > 3% => FAIL.
- Silent fallback > 1% absolute in canonical set => FAIL.
- p95 latency increase > 20% for production batch sizes => FAIL.

Evaluation harness & automation:
- Use the existing invocation harness (invocation-eval-runner) but add a small wrapper to apply perturbations and record intermediate states (selected tool, raw model output, parsed args, downstream tool call outcome).
- Record metadata: model commit/tag, quantization profile, serving runtime kernel selection, batch config, region.
- Output format: newline-delimited JSONL artifacts (used elsewhere) with fields flattened (we will keep a small CSV summary for quick triage).
- Regression gating: harness posts results to Linear ticket (INV-402) and to /eng-applied-ml Slack channel if any FAIL conditions met.

Sample failure cases (from preliminary runs):
1) Multi-step weather+calendar chain: model invoked http-fetch with the right endpoint but returned args as a single concatenated string for "date_range" instead of {"start":"2025-02-10","end":"2025-02-12"}. The downstream calendar parser returned a 400. Transcript attached (redacted).
2) Ambiguous prompt with filler noise: user says "book a meeting with Alex, also check flights" — model selected calendar and also emitted a HTTP tool with partial JSON missing closing brace. This caused silent fallback in 12% of noise variants.
3) Batching regression: at batch size 8, KV-cache eviction timing changed and occasionally produced earlier-step tokens in current output leading to mangled args. Occurred for a quantized kernel path.

Triage rubric (quick):
- If TSA failed but arg-parse still intact -> consider prompt-clarity augmentation + example-based calibration.
- If arg-parse broke consistently across perturbations -> examine tokenizer alignment and serializing codepath that maps model text -> JSON. Add stricter parsing and fallback validation.
- If failure only at higher batch sizes -> instrument runtime (kernel selection, cache management) and revert batch config for Canary.

Remediation experiments (short list):
- Add 6 shot examples demonstrating both correct tool selection and JSON payload formatting for the ambiguous cases. Measure effect on TSA and arg F1.
- Tighten the post-process parser to run JSON sanitizer + schema validation; on parse failure, ask model for clarification (controlled fallback).
- Kernel-level experiment: force alternate matmul kernel selection for the quantized path and re-run the batch sweep.

Rollout & gating proposal:
- Canary stage: deploy ModelX-v2 to 5% of traffic for hosted with evaluation hook enabled (run the harness on sampled invocations).
- Dedicated staging: deploy to a dedicated pool with identical config; run the full suite nightly for 7 days.
- Gate: do not increase dedicated commit capacity or enable burst config until no FAILs seen for 72 hours on nightly runs and TSA/arg F1 within thresholds.

Operational playbook (if FAIL during canary):
1) Automated alert -> notify on-call applied-ml engineer + SRE.
2) Pull recent eval artifacts from storage bucket and run local failing examples.
3) Toggle model routing to previous stable variant for affected routes.
4) Triage and PR with fix; re-run harness on staging.

Instrumentation & logging needs (action items):
- ensure invocation-harness logs raw model outputs alongside parsed args (privacy filter applied).
- add a small schema validator that records field-level mismatches to help identify common patterns (e.g., quoting issues, single-string vs structured).
- expose a quick query in Console to pull the top-10 failing transcripts for a model-version.

Checklist (next 2 weeks):
- [ ] Finalize canonical prompt set (Jordan, Priya) — target 2025-02-18.
- [ ] Implement perturbation wrapper in invocation-eval-runner (Marco) — target 2025-02-20.
- [ ] Add schema validator to postprocessing (Riley) — target 2025-02-22.
- [ ] Run first nightly sweep on dedicated staging (Jordan) — target 2025-02-24.
- [ ] Review failures and produce patch or prompt templates (team) — target 2025-02-28.

Open questions / unknowns:
- How representative are the telemetry-derived prompts for enterprise customers who use long, policy-heavy contexts? We might need an "enterprise augment" set.
- Do we want to gate on absolute thresholds or relative to a rolling baseline (models will slowly improve/hurt across many small commits)?
- Is the proposed silent-fallback threshold (1%) too strict for new model families?

Notes to self / rough ideas:
- Could add a small adversarial set where an assistant is instructed to "hide" arguments in parentheses or in code blocks to see parser brittleness.
- Consider adding a human-in-the-loop quick labeler to inspect top-50 failing transcripts weekly.

Attachments / useful links:
- linear:INV-402 (tracking harness work)
- gh:serving-runtime#1297 (batch-kernel experiment)
- confluence:Onboarding/ModelX-evals (current baseline prompts)

If you want, I can convert this into a runnable checklist and create the Linear subtasks for the 2-week items. Leaving rough TODOs inline.

-- Jordan
